topic: EXP-640: firmament height consistency patches in data/sections.json part7 (770,000->~820,000; 8,537 km at pole+rim)

holes_found.description: EXP-640 Patch 2 updated the body text to '(8,537 km at the pole; ~837 km at the rim)' but left the §7.4 TLDR summary unchanged. The TLDR still reads: 'Multiple spacecraft have orbited above the dome's claimed firmament height (8,500 km) and found no boundary'. A casual reader scanning TLDRs sees 8,500 km while the body text now says 8,537 km at the pole. This is a minor inconsistency introduced by the partial-scope patch.
holes_found.proposed_fix: In the §7.4 ps-tldr paragraph, replace '(8,500 km)' with '(8,537 km at the pole)' to match the body text and §7.2 convention.

summary_for_decider: EXP-640 landed correctly — both patches confirmed present, old strings absent. Ratio arithmetic: 7×10⁹ km / 8,537 km = 819,960 ≈ ~820,000 ✓. The 2 remaining 9,086 occurrences in part7 are in a separate context (WIN-017 wobble math at arctan(20/9,086,000)) and are not the patched New Horizons citation — legitimate. One minor hole: the §7.4 ps-tldr summary still says '(8,500 km)' while the body now says '(8,537 km at the pole; ~837 km at the rim)'. One-line fix: replace '(8,500 km)' in the TLDR with '(8,537 km at the pole)'. Decider can self-apply at next run.

check_detail.check1_terminology: 8,537 km convention now appears 7× in part7 body, consistently with §7.2. However, the §7.4 ps-tldr still carries '(8,500 km)' — see holes_found. The Gaia TLDR (§7.3) 'within 8,500 km on a firmament' is a general bound (not pole-specific) and is conservatively correct at 8,500 < 8,537; not flagged as a hole.
check_detail.check2_seam_artifacts: No double-periods (0), double-commas (0), or orphan semicolons (0) in part7 html. Both patch seams are clean.
check_detail.check3_patches_landed: patches_checked=2, patches_landed=2. Patch 1: old '770,000 times the dome\'s maximum firmament height (9,086 km)' count=0; new '~820,000 times the dome\'s maximum firmament height (8,537 km at the pole)' count=1. Patch 2: old '(8,500 km at equator)' count=0; new '(8,537 km at the pole; ~837 km at the rim)' count=1.
check_detail.check5_adversarial: Patch 1 sentence: 'approximately ~820,000 times' has a mild redundancy ('approximately' + '~') but this is consistent with pre-existing prose style in the section and is not a new defect. Ratio math verified: 7,000,000,000 / 8,537 = 819,960 ≈ 820,000 ✓ (old ratio 770,000 was 7e9/9,086 ≈ 770,416 ✓). Patch 2 parenthetical '(8,537 km at the pole; ~837 km at the rim)' strengthens the argument by showing satellites orbit above dome at both pole and rim; ISS at 408 km below dome at pole reading is correct. No double-negatives, no broken citations.
